Comments: This inspection report has been developed to document an on-site routine complete inspect, and to summarize the overall status of this well and well location. The project was recently acquired by Big Dog Energy, LLC. Applications for the transfer of all five wells permitted on the site, from Geopetro LLC to Big Dog Energy LLC, were received by the Department on August 2, 2021. An application for the transfer of the ESCGP that is currently active on the site was also received by the Department. The current Operator information has not yet been updated in the Department's electronic database. Well number 019-21928, along with four other wells, (API ID#'s: 019-21907, 019-21929, 019-21931, 019-21932), were drilled and currently exist on the location. Although the Act Nine sign has been changed to reflect the current owner of the well location, the well tags have not yet been updated. Updated well tags should be installed on each of the wells at some point in the near future. Inspection ID number's 2139667, 2139736, 2139741, 2199744 and 2139746, (conducted on February 13, 2013), suggests that all of the wells have been stimulated. Subsequent inspections indicate that that the wells have been on inactive status since at least March of 2014. ESCGP number ESX11-019-0091 is currently active on the site. The permit was renewed by RE Gas in 2017 and is set to expire on 09/15/2022. None of the earthwork proposed in the plan was ever implemented in the field. The location consists of one very large well location and a separate tank pad. The location is overgrown and clearly has not been tended to in any way for some time. There are currently, however, no clear E&S or stabilization-related issues associated with the site.

Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8251226
Permit API: 129-26172
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Oklahoma Borough
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/02/2025
Comments: On October 2 2025, the Department conducted a complaint inspection in regards to CTS 392648. This gas well is currently under an Order (Enf ID 442909). This inspection is not evaluating the operator's compliance with the Order and is being conducted in response to the aforementioned complaint.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the access road and well site appeared to be stabilized with no accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well appeared equipped for production. A well tag was present on the well head and a well posting was present on a piece of the production equipment. There were no observed fluid leaks observed coming from the well head.Upon inspection of the production tank, the Department observed piping which ran to/from the production tank and the valve near the bottom of the tank, both of which appeared to be heavily corroded. It appeared a small about of fluid was seeping from the corroded portions of the piping onto the ground. The Department obtained a conductivity reading of the fluid on the pipe of 3.07mS. The Department obtained conductivity readings in the gravel below the corroded piping of 1.73ms and 0.87ms in an approximately 1 foot radius from the valve at the bottom of the production tank. These readings appear elevated in comparison to the Department's background conductivity reading of 0.22mS, indicating a release of production fluids has/is occurring.Prior to leaving the site, the Department attempted to contact the operator by calling the phone number on the well tag. Violation ID: 8154334
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the EQT - Phoenix Pad S on 6/10/20 @1200 hours in response to CTS report#350244 regarding the reported release of 15 gallons of produced fluid from an evaporation unit. The weather was 79 degrees, partly cloudy, humidity 78%, with scattered showers and thunderstorms in the area. The winds were SSW @9mph. No activity or personnel was observe onsite. Multiple areas that appeared slightly damp below the surface were tested for field conductivity and found to be 0.09mS/cm and 0.15mS/cm. No additional areas of concern were identified. The spill appears to have been adequately remediated. A large disturbed area off the SE corner of the well pad appears to consist of a berm and standing water. The area appears stabilized with mulch and CFS. It is not clear if this area is a PCSM BMP or a pipeline issue. Violations cited against API#117-21115 are cited as immediately corrected. I departed the site @1300 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 7/29/2025 to EQT PROD CO in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland county. 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT PROD CO
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/29/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8242704
Permit API: 129-29266
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Allegheny Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/29/2025
Comments: On July 29, 2025, the DEP conducted an Incident Inspection of EQTs Porter Well Pad located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 7/28/2025 at 2:54 pm.The spill report stated that at 2:06 pm on 7/28/2025, over 5 gallons of production fluids were found on the gravel well pad at the Porter Well site after removing secondary containment. Accompanying during today's inspection is EQTs representative Kyle Borden.At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed an Act 9 Sign posted at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it. In the on-site mailbox, the DEP observed both an Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan, that had different Operator information on it than the Act 9 sign. The DEP recommends the Operator update the plans as applicable. At the time of this inspection, drill outs were recently completed on the 6U and containment was removed from the well pad the day prior. Mr. Borden stated that the secondary containment in the release area was packed with tanks and large equipment, therefore despite routine inspections of the containment, only the edges of the containment could be inspected, and no holes or tears were observed. However, upon removal of the containment, staining and small puddles were observed on the gravel pad in an approximately 115 ft x 60 ft area. At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed the area of the graveled pad where this incident occurred to be adjacent to wellheads covered by boxes. The pea gravel in this area was observed to be wet with sections that appeared to be darker in color than other areas. Mr. Borden stated that SPSI and Moody were arriving on site to remediate the release and that they estimate remediation to be completed within the day. EQT representative Schuyler Brounce mentioned in his email (documented in IR 4024285), that following his review of the incident, he estimates the release to be over 1 barrel. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Borden stated once all contaminated gravel has been removed, an updated quantity will be provided to the DEP.At the time of this inspection, the DEP utilized a conductivity meter to screen the graveled well pad. The DEP collected soil readings of 1.835 mS, 3.22 mS, 3.35 mS and 2.08 mS in the incident area closest to the wellheads, as well as 2.56 mS between two wellheads and a fluid reading of Over Range in fluid observed to be pooled in secondary containment adjacent to the release area. These conductivity readings are elevated when compared to the background soil reading of 0.1457 mS collected in vegetation by the Act 9 Sign.At the time of this inspection, the DEP requested secondary containment logs for the Porter well pad and Mr. Borden stated they would be provided to the Department electronically. The DEP is also requesting an electronic copy of the Safety Data Sheets for all chemicals stored/utilized within and near the secondary containment that was observed to have the release underneath by COB 8/5/2025.The DEP recommends the Operator promptly remediate the release in accordance with 78a.66(c)(2).Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the over 1 barrel release of production fluids on the graveled well pad.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 days of the receipt of this report. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, a plan for remediation of the violations and how the Operator quantified the amount released. The Operator will need to follow Act 2 guidelines as set by 78a.66(c)(2) and assess the impacts to the Water of the Commonwealth from the release.

Permit API: 129-27948
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/14/2024
Comments: On 3/14/2024 OGI Geoffrey Lutty conducted an onsite inspection of the Martin 2 gas well, API 129-27948. The well appeared equipped for production. The well displayed moderate corrosion. The well name and API was scratched into a pipe clamp, this does not meet the posting requirements of 3211(G). The line leading to the production tank appears to have failed and separated. A second tank was unused onsite as seen in the photographs, it is recommended to remove this equipment under OGA 3216(c). OGI used a Bascom Turner EGA 611 and detected multiple gas leaks. Gas was leaking from the base of the wellhead as seen in the attached photographs at 12%LEL. The line leading into the production tank appears to have separated and was leaking gas at 79%Gas. The soils in a 2' radius around the failed connected were tested and gas was detected at a peak of 31%LEL in the soils at 3" depth. No 2023 APR is on record, the latest record is from 2022 and indicates production. No 2023 MIA is on record, the latest record is from 2022. Based on todays inspection the following violations will be issued: OGA3211(G) - Failure to install permit number and operator information. 78.88(a) - Failure to inspect well quarterly for Mechanical Integrity Assessment. 78.88(b)1-4 - Failure to meet minimum requirements for inspections. 78.88(e) - Failure to submit annual report to the Department for Mechanical Integrity Assessments. 78.121(A) - Failure to submit annual production report. 78.121(B) - Failure to electronically submit Annual Production Report to the Department. 78.88(d) - Failure to notify the Department and take corrective action to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion or other signs of deterioration that compromises the integrity of the well. 78.73(a) - Failure to operate the well in accordance with 25 PA code Chapter 78 and ensure the integrity of the well is maintained. 78.74 - Venting of gas to the atmosphere that produces a hazard to public health and safety.

Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to the notification by Cliff Easton of Consortium Energy of a crude oil release from a buried gathering line located approximately 150 feet to the south of this conventional well.Upon my arrival onsite, Cliff and I evaluated the section of roadside ditch where oil was discovered, which is within approximately ten feet of an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Turnup Run. The gathering lines for the Warrant 3410 lease are located within this ditch, therefore a failure of one of these lines is the likely culprit. Consortium has shut in all of the wells on the lease and has placed absorbent pads and peat across the ditch floor to prevent any appreciable oil from reaching the stream. At this time, only a slight emulsion is present in the UNT of Turnup Run, no sheen or free product was observed upon agitating the stream. It appears that the released crude oil remains in the soil within the ditch. Booms and pads have been placed at the inlet and near the outlet of a culvert that carries the stream across the lease road as a precaution. Consortium was coordinating with local contractors to begin excavating the contaminated soil and confirm/repair the source of the release. I advised Cliff to maintain the containment in the ditch and to regularly check the booms in the UNT of Turnup Run. If any appreciable amount of oil is discovered in the stream, please contact the Department. Cliff stated that production would not continue on the lease until the lines in this ditch are repaired or replaced.Upcoming inspections will be conducted to evaluate remediation efforts and if there is any additional impact to the UNT of Turnup Run.

Inspection Date: 3/26/2021
Comments: This spill occurred sometime in the previous few months but was not reported to DEP. It was noted on a routine inspection by WQSS Rob Bechtel and myself en route to check another site. It appears as though a line leaked and allowed an unknown quantity of crude oil to be released to the site. Some volume flowed off the site and entered a spring run/UNT of Twomile Run. Crude oil was apparent in pools in several areas and fresher product was caught in moss lining the channel of the spring. It then appears to have flowed some 300 feet and entered another UNT of Twomile Run. The operator placed a boom in this stream at some point prior to the discovery of this spill by myself. Some sheen was apparent in leaf piles at this point, but no fresh product was noted. The operator was contacted and they were on the lease at the time. Immediate cleanup options were discussed, including installation of two siphon dams in the initial spring run and use of absorbent pads to catch any oil seeping from the banks. Further inspection will be performed as necessary. Violations are noted.

The 2H had no water at ground level. I met with CALLC Field Rep. Craig Shores and Creston Consultant Reps., Kevin Leaman and Andrew Pfisterer. Starting at approx. 07:15 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. - Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below: - 1H (16x11) annulus: Not sure which annulus has gas due to single cap covering the (16x11 and 11x8) annuli. **see (11x8) annulus for results** (11x8) annulus: 2 psi.; 100% gas, Sample taken @ 07:30 ** Pressure in the (16x8) shared vent appears to be a new occurrence since last PBUT on 11/18/2021.** (8x5) annulus: 0 psi.; 50% gas, Sample taken @ 07:35 - 2H (16x11): annulus is cemented over (11x8) annulus: 25 psi.; 100% gas, Sample taken @ 07:50 (8x5) annulus: 0 psi.; 25,420 ppm dropping to 0% gas, No sample taken - Both wells annuli were returned to open and venting to temporary poly tanks @ 08:10. ** Due to the probable impact of these wells defective conditions on the on going gas migration in the area, if not corrected, additional violations may be issued.

Conductivity readings taken during this inspection indicate that a small area of contaminated soil remains to be removed upslope from the current excavation area. When the remaining contaminated soil has been removed, fresh topsoil should be used to fill in this area, and mulch should be used to stabilize the area for the winter. Seed will then be needed in the spring. After evaluating the site this morning with Wilbur Carney and Brian Stanford of DE LTD, a determination was made that the spill volume appears to be less than one barrel of produced fluid. This site should be remediated as a visual cleanup.

Comments: On March 9, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt's Armstrong 2 well located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following Complaint Inspection 3891447 where violations were issued for inadequate stabilization of the direct and shared portions of the access road that leads to the Armstrong 2 site. A notice of violation (NOV) operator response has yet to be received from the Operator of this Oil and Gas well following IR 3891447, however, a NOV response was received for a nearby well site operated by a separate Operator that received the same violations for the shared portion of the Armstrong 2's access road, and that NOV response stated that repairs to the shared portion of the road would be conducted in the Spring of 2025.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the condition of the shared portion of Wildcat Road to be worse than what was observed during the Department's last inspection (IR 3990630), major rutting, mud puddles and erosion rills were observed throughout. Wildcat Road eventually leads to a fork, left leading to another well site (the JC Armstrong Jr 1), and right leading directly to the Armstrong 2 well site. Along the direct portions of the Armstrong 2 well site, the Department observed large areas of the access road to be flooded. An exposed pipe was observed alongside the access road, however no methane or other odor was detected, the exposed portion of the pipe did not appear to be compromised. A well tag was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted gas well with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the surface of the gas well at this time. A heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank at this time. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank to ensure the corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release. Violations are being issued in a separate inspection report for the heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release.Based on today's inspection, violations issued for an inadequately stabilized access road is to remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a FUI inspection at the Tilden Marcellus LLC - Simonetti 801 located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 10/2/2019 @0845 hours. The weather was sunny 74 degrees. Onsite for the inspection was myself, Korey Starkey, DEP WQS; Jennifer Compton and Nathan Smelser, Tilden Marcellus; Farm Boy Excavation; Civil and Environmental Consultants, Inc. As of today's inspection, a large stain was observed on the gravel surface adjacent to the failed dump line measuring ~8'x4'(See Photo#1). Tilden's earthmoving contractor, Farm Boy, had used a small excavator to scrape the surface of the impacted pad area, fill slope (see photo #2) and dig a sump in the fill slope approximately 4' wide and 5' deep. Fluid that had accumulated in the bottom of the sump had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm(See Photo#3). Sample 4427-192 was collected from the fluid in the fill slope sump and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for SAC 942 analysis. CEC consultants had delineated the extent of the impacted area with white flags. The excavator, and CEC, were currently working to remove soil with an elevated conductivity in an area below the toe of the fill slope(See Photo#4,5). The excavated sump was then expanded across the fill slope. A wet gravel layer was observed ~3' below the pad surface that appeared to be the source of the >19.99mS/cm fluid entering the sump(See Photo#6). Jennifer Compton and CEC continued to screen the fill slope area and remove additional material. The impacted material was being staged on the pad surface, on the interior of the gas line, awaiting the delivery of more disposal boxes. Ms. Compton was also awaiting the delivery of a super sucker truck to remove additional pad material. Tilden Marcellus and CEC were advised to contact the DEP Environment Cleanups and Brownfields (ECB) Program to facilitate cleanup activities going forward. Violations cited previously in inspection report#2939891, dated 9/30/2019 are cited as OUTSTANDING against the 2H well, API#117-20309 at this time. We departed the site @1200 hours. - Invalid Complaint Id. - 345263

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 3/04/2021
Comments: On 03/04/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted a follow-up inspection at Chesapeake Appalachia LLC’s (CALLC) STONE location. The purpose of this inspection was to document the status of the site and visually observe the location of a previous release of production / flowback fluids. Details regarding the release can be found within inspection report (IR) # 3141162 & 3144646. I arrived at 1232 hours. The weather was 31 degrees with overcast skies. Slopes around the site had approximately 2 – 4 inches of snow cover present. Majority of the pad surface had puddles present. At the time of this inspection, there were 2 roll-off containers labelled as "BRINE" stationed within a shared secondary containment (photo # 2). The release detailed in IR # 3141162 appears to have occurred west of the currently stationed roll-off containers, based on photos within the report. Puddles on the pad surface around the roll-off containers’ secondary containment was screened for field measured specific conductivity using an OAKTON PCTS 50 meter. Puddles immediately adjacent to the western edge of the containment ranged from 1010 uS/cm – 2.56 mS/cm (photo # 4, 6, 8). Higher readings appeared to trend off the NW corner of the containment. Fluid within containment was screened at 14.88 mS/cm (photo # 14). A visual inspection of the containment did not reveal any obvious deficiencies. I called Eric Hottenstein (CALLC, HSE Supervisor) at 1313 hours in order to discuss my findings. Mr. Hottenstein stated a vacuum truck would be sent out in order to vacuum the pad and CALLC would investigate the origin of the cause of the elevated conductivity readings. Violations cited within IR # 3141162 remain in the outstanding status against well permit # 015-23632. I departed the site at 1330 hours.

Violation ID: 8267111
Permit API: 051-23265
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Springhill Township
Inspection Type: Site Restoration
Inspection Date: 3/05/2026
Comments: On March 5, 2026, the Department conducted a Site Restoration Inspection of Diversified's Robinson 13 plugged well site located in Springhill Township, Fayette County following the receipt of a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) on 1/28/26.A COA was entered into between the Department and Diversified on March 7, 2019. According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216. Violations were issued during IR 4156278 for failure to comply with a COA of the Department.According to Department records, this well was plugged on 4/3/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 1/3/2026 and a well site restoration report be submitted to the Department by 3/4/2026. At the time of this inspection, the Department did not observe a Post-Plugging Site Restoration Plan along the shared access road, the direct access road or the plugged well site. Violations are being issued at this time for failure to have a post-plugging site restoration plan on site. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the direct portion of the access road that leads to the plugged well site to be a partially vegetated dirt road with muddy tire tracks throughout. These tire tracks continue onto the plugged well site. At the time of this inspection, the plugged well site appeared to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth everywhere except where the tire tracks were observed. Compost Filter Sock appeared to be spread along the perimeters of the plugged well site. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the approximate GPS location of the plugged well. No equipment associated with the plugging of the well or the plugged well site was observed at this time. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure to have the site restoration plan on site. The WSRR is being returned at this time due to the plugged well site and access road not appearing to be restored.
